Thanks for the context, Soojin.

Quick assessment from Finance/AR: quarterly invoicing is operationally fine (we can schedule 4 invoices/year). Net-90, however, increases DSO materially and introduces credit risk for a new customer without payment history. Options to consider:

- Compromise A: Offer Net-60 with quarterly invoicing and standard 30-day payment on future expansions.
- Compromise B: Approve Net-90 but require one of the following upfront: signed PO + ACH/ACH token or 30% upfront deposit, and limit Net-90 to the first 2–3 invoices while we validate payment behavior.
- If we grant Net-90 with no upfront deposits, we should limit discount to <= 10% and add a past-due interest clause (1.5% monthly) and credit hold triggers.

From a discount perspective: a 15% discount is on the high side for a payment-terms concession. Finance would accept up to 10% with the constraints above and an exec approval for Net-90.

Please attach the SOW in HubSpot and include the PO when you have it. I can draft the payment-term language for Contracts if the team decides to proceed.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Revenue Operations & Finance Integrations
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Invoice cadence and payment terms request for Orion — Approval

Appreciate the triage. I approve the following for Orion Analytics to close the deal this quarter:

1) Invoicing cadence: quarterly (4 invoices per year) as requested.
2) Payment terms: Net-90 for the first three invoices only. If all three invoices clear on time, we will move to Net-60 for subsequent invoices.
3) Discount: approve up to 10% as a one-time commercial concession, not a recurring price change.
4) Conditions: require signed SOW, signed PO, and ACH setup (token or direct debit) before first invoice. Add 1.5% monthly late fee and credit-hold trigger on 60 days past due.

Please update the HubSpot deal (DL-2026-0897) with these terms, attach the SOW and payment schedule, and route to Contracts to bake the language into the SOW/Order Form. Finance (Vanessa) — please prepare the payment-term addendum and queue the billing schedule.

Sophie — if that works for Orion, Soojin can confirm and we will proceed to finalize the paperwork. Happy to jump on a short call if you want to tighten the milestones.
